summary: Builds a row-major 3x3 rotation matrix at `this` (nine consecutive doubles at offsets 0x0 through 0x40) from the three Euler angles in `a2` using the standard sin/cos composition. Purely mathematical, no branches, no callees. Used by vehicle physics orientation paths (suspension setup, vehicle physics init, rigid body constraint solve, rotation-tensor transform).

local_names.this: output 3x3 rotation matrix, nine doubles at 0x0..0x40
local_names.a2: input Euler angle triple (x, y, z)

operations.description: Compute the six sine/cosine terms of the three input Euler angles a2, a2[1], a2[2]
Precompute the two combined terms v10 = cos(z)*cos(y) and v9 = sin(z)*cos(y) used across matrix rows
Write matrix element at this+0x0 (row 0 col 0) = sin(y)*sin(x)*sin(z) + cos(z)*cos(y)
Write matrix element at this+0x8 (row 0 col 1) = sin(y)*sin(x)*cos(z) - sin(z)*cos(y)
Write matrix element at this+0x10 (row 0 col 2) = sin(y)*cos(x)
Write matrix element at this+0x18 (row 1 col 0) = sin(z)*cos(x)
Write matrix element at this+0x20 (row 1 col 1) = cos(z)*cos(x)
Write matrix element at this+0x28 (row 1 col 2) = -sin(x)
Write matrix element at this+0x30 (row 2 col 0) = sin(z)*cos(y)*sin(x) - cos(z)*sin(y)
Write matrix element at this+0x38 (row 2 col 1) = sin(z)*sin(y) + cos(z)*cos(y)*sin(x)
Write matrix element at this+0x40 (row 2 col 2) = cos(y)*cos(x)
Return the input angle pointer a2
